content.name: Basics of National Income Accounting
content.description: This course offers a comprehensive introduction to the principles of national income accounting. It is designed for public officials who require a solid grasp of macroeconomic indicators to inform their work in policy-making, financial management, and economic analysis. The course begins by explaining the importance of measuring economic activity and introduces the circular flow of income model to illustrate the interactions between households, firms, and the government. You will delve into the core concepts of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), exploring its definition and significance. The curriculum details the three primary methods for measuring GDP: the output (or production) method, the income method, and the expenditure method. Furthermore, the course clarifies the critical distinction between nominal and real GDP, explaining how inflation is accounted for to provide a true measure of economic growth. You will also learn about related concepts like Gross National Product (GNP) and Gross Value Added (GVA), and how these metrics are used to compare economic performance across sectors and countries. Upon completion, you will be equipped to interpret key economic statistics and understand their implications for governance and national development.

content.name: Reviving Yantra India Limited: Leading Change in PSU
content.description: Yantra India Limited (YIL), formed in 2021 from eight Ordnance Factories, aimed to boost India’s defence manufacturing but faced major hurdles in its transition from a government setup to a corporate entity. With limited orders, a ₹1230 million loss, and low employee morale, the company struggled to stay afloat. The end of overtime pay, manpower shortages, and financial strain deepened challenges. YIL secured a small order from Indian Railways and credit from SBI but needed stronger momentum. Its leadership now faces critical choices—whether to expand exports, diversify products, or enhance customer ties—while motivating employees and balancing cost control with welfare to ensure long-term survival.
content.provider: Capacity Building Commission
content.instructions:
Yantra India Limited (YIL), a Defence Public Sector Undertaking under the Ministry of Defence, was formed on August 14, 2021, by converting eight Ordnance Factories and a Training Institute from the Ordnance Factory Board. It began operations on October 1, 2021, to strengthen India’s defence preparedness. However, the shift from a government setup to a corporate structure brought serious challenges, including financial losses, limited orders, and a demotivated workforce.

The Ordnance Factory Board had long struggled with issues of quality, high costs, and delays. To improve efficiency, the government reorganized it into seven new defence companies, including YIL. With only ₹180 million in orders over three years, YIL soon faced a loss of ₹1230 million within six months. The transition created uncertainty and low morale among employees, especially after the removal of overtime pay. Despite assurances that service conditions would remain protected, resistance grew, and productivity suffered.

YIL also struggled with manpower shortages as new functions like Quality and Finance had to be managed internally. To ease pressure, staff were brought in from a less busy factory in Jabalpur. Financially, YIL faced a cash crunch due to its small order book but managed to secure credit support from SBI. Meanwhile, efforts to secure railway orders showed limited success, with only a small order won after considerable effort.

The leadership now faces tough choices whether to expand exports, diversify products, or strengthen customer relations to stabilize finances. It must also find ways to motivate employees without overtime, possibly through incentives or better engagement, while balancing cost cuts with job security. YIL’s future depends on innovative decisions, financial prudence, and its ability to build a motivated and resilient workforce.

content.name: Haryana Civil Services Government Employees Conduct Rules 2016
content.description: This course provides a detailed examination of the Haryana Civil Services Conduct Rules of 2016, a critical framework for ensuring integrity and professionalism in public administration. The program is structured to give learners a thorough understanding of their duties and limitations as government employees. It begins by defining the scope and applicability of the rules, establishing a foundation for ethical conduct. Key learning areas include a deep dive into what constitutes misconduct, with specific guidance on prohibited actions to avoid disciplinary issues. The course places special emphasis on sensitive topics such as restrictions on political activities, employment of relatives in private undertakings, and interactions with the media. Furthermore, it clarifies regulations concerning financial transactions, acceptance of gifts, and the declaration of assets and liabilities, promoting transparency and accountability. By completing this course, government employees will be equipped to uphold the highest standards of professional conduct, make sound ethical judgments, and contribute to a more transparent and effective governance system in Haryana.

content.name: Introduction to Industry 4.0 and Digital Transformation
content.description: Industry 4.0 is reshaping the landscape of manufacturing and public services by integrating physical operations with smart, digital technologies. This course serves as a comprehensive introduction to the principles and applications of this industrial transformation. You will delve into the key enabling technologies, including the Internet of Things (IoT) for data collection, Artificial Intelligence (AI) for process optimization, and cloud computing for scalable data management. The course explains the architecture of a smart factory, where cyber-physical systems communicate in real-time to support autonomous and predictive operations. Through practical examples, you will learn how these innovations are applied to solve real-world challenges like predictive maintenance, quality control, and supply chain optimization. By the end of this course, you will have a clear framework for understanding the impact of Industry 4.0 and be able to identify opportunities for digital transformation within your own organizational context, recognizing both the potential benefits and the implementation challenges.

content.name: Navigating DPDP: The Future of Digital Governance in India
content.description: This policy-focused course delves into the practical implementation of the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023, within government institutions. It provides a critical examination of the framework's core components, including exemptions for state functions under Section 17 and the delicate balance between citizen rights and public accountability. The discussion addresses significant operational challenges, such as institutional readiness gaps, the enforcement role of the Data Protection Board, and data breach notification responsibilities. Learners will gain insights into managing shared accountability for large-scale digital platforms like Aadhaar and DigiLocker, structuring contracts with IT vendors, and handling cross-border data flows. Furthermore, the course explores the intersection of DPDP with AI-driven automated decision-making and bias in public systems. It concludes by outlining a strategic readiness roadmap to help senior officials strengthen data governance, build institutional capacity, and enhance citizen trust in the evolving digital ecosystem.

content.name: Geospatial Data Analysis with LiDAR and GNSS
content.description: This course provides a comprehensive understanding of LiDAR, GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite Systems), and AI/ML approaches for satellite data analysis. Participants will learn how LiDAR laser pulses are transmitted, how their reflections are received, and the type of information that can be extracted from this point-based data. The course explains how to process vast amounts of LiDAR data and generate digital elevation models for analyzing land features and underwater terrain. Through the example of GPS, learners will understand the planning and processing of GNSS missions, as well as common errors that may occur. The course further explores AI and ML architectures, demonstrating how these techniques can be applied to satellite data for practical use cases such as crop mapping, crop yield estimation, land use/land cover assessment, deforestation monitoring, and ship detection.

In today’s highly digital and interconnected environment, applications represent one of the primary attack surfaces for cyber threats, making robust application security a critical component of organisational cybersecurity strategy. The course focuses on integrating security into technology, processes, governance, and organisational culture. Participants will learn about secure coding practices, threat modelling, vulnerability management, runtime protections, and security integration within CI/CD pipelines. It also explores the importance of aligning application security initiatives with industry frameworks such as OWASP and NIST, while addressing compliance and governance requirements.

  • Apply secure coding practices, threat modelling, and vulnerability management techniques during software development.
  • Explain the role of CI/CD pipelines, automated security testing, and shift-left security approaches in reducing production vulnerabilities.

  • Implement security measures for APIs, cloud-native applications, containers, and third-party software components.

content.name: Concept of Privacy and Evolution of Data Protection Rights
content.description: This course introduces learners to the concept of privacy as a fundamental human right and a constitutionally protected right in India, tracing its evolution from traditional notions of personal liberty to contemporary concerns in the digital age. It examines the meaning and dimensions of privacy, including the right to be let alone, freedom from unwarranted publicity, and protection against unwarranted interference in private life. The course explores the international legal framework governing privacy, including Article 12 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948), Article 17 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR), and Article 8 of the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR).

content.name: Data Privacy Compliance Scoping under DPDPA ISO 27001 and ISO 27701
content.description:
This course provides a practitioner-level guide to scoping data privacy compliance projects under ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27701, and India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDPA). Using a structured 22-question scoping questionnaire, it explains how to define organisational boundaries, identify in-scope geographies, data principals, departments, applications, and third-party vendors, and assess the maturity of existing privacy controls. The course includes real-world scope statements for a State Transport Department, State Health Department, and Municipal Corporation, illustrating how Data Fiduciaries determine their DPDPA obligations. It also presents a 12-month, five-phase implementation roadmap covering gap assessment, policy framework development, DPIA, third-party risk assessment, and implementation activities including breach reporting, consent management, Privacy by Design, and DPO governance. 
Target Audience: Data Protection Officer

content.name: Privacy-Enhancing Technologies and Data Protection Practices
content.description: This course explores Privacy-Enhancing Technologies (PETs) from the perspective of a Data Protection Officer, with a focus on safeguarding personal data in both static and dynamic environments. It introduces the critical distinction between data at rest and data in motion, along with the corresponding technical and organizational safeguards applicable to each. The course examines advanced cryptographic PETs, including Homomorphic Encryption (Partial, Somewhat, and Fully Homomorphic), Secure Multi-Party Computation using Shamir’s Secret Sharing, and Zero-Knowledge Proofs, highlighting their real-world applications in blockchain, authentication, and voting systems. It also covers Federated Learning for privacy-preserving AI model training across decentralized environments and Differential Privacy for protecting individuals in aggregated datasets.

content.name: MANTHAN: Building India's Demand-Driven Industry-Academia Bridge
content.description:
Manthan is a digital platform launched on 15 August 2022 by the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser (PSA) to the Government of India, under the leadership of Professor Ajay Kumar Sood.  It was designed to bridge a persistent structural gap in India's innovation ecosystem: organisations with technical, social, or commercial problems could not easily find research institutions, startups, or innovators with relevant solutions, and vice versa.

The case traces a central dilemma: could a digital platform, even one backed by the institutional credibility of the PSA's office, shift the entrenched behaviours, reliance on personal networks, premier-institution bias, and risk-averse CSR decision-making that had long sustained the industry-academia gap? The case concludes with the platform's most unresolved challenge: despite facilitating thousands of crores in research investment, it faced a one-crore annual maintenance gap that threatened its continuity.

content.name: Digital Shift in Urban Accounting : Karnataka's Municipal Finance
content.description:
Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) are critical to city-level service delivery, making sound financial management essential for informed decision-making. In Karnataka, municipal accounting followed the Karnataka Municipal Accounting Manual, 1965, prescribing a manual, single-entry, cash-based system. Delays in revenue data, inconsistent figures and weak financial visibility limited effective management.

Recognising that credible governance depends on credible financial data, Karnataka introduced the Fund Based Accrual Accounting System (FBAAS) in 2006. Based on ICAI principles, FBAAS strengthened financial tracking, transparency and compliance by classifying municipal resources into governmental, proprietary and fiduciary funds. Its integration with Khajane 2 and e-Sweekruthi enabled seamless information flows across departments. This case examines how accounting reform, institutional ownership and digital integration can transform municipal financial governance.
content.provider: Capacity Building Commission
content.instructions:
From the case study, participants will be able to:

  • Understand the limitations of manual, cash-based municipal accounting and the rationale for transitioning to Fund Based Accrual Accounting.
  • Explain how FBAAS integrates accounting, budgeting, revenue collection, expenditure control and financial reporting to strengthen fiscal discipline and transparency.
  • Analyse the integration of FBAAS with e-Sweekruthi and Khajane 2, and its role in creating seamless, real-time financial workflows.
  • Assess the institutional, technological and capacity-building challenges involved in implementing large-scale digital accounting reforms.
  • Examine how digital financial systems can embed accountability, improve audit readiness and support data-driven decision-making.
  • Apply the lessons from Karnataka’s experience to identify suitable financial management reforms for their own ULBs.
  • Recognise that sustainable digital transformation requires institutional ownership, standardisation, phased implementation and continuous capacity building.
